learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Demonstrate the capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Demonstrate skills for planning, organization, and strategy.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Possess solid knowledge that allows oral and written communication in a foreign language, preferably English.
Possess knowledge of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT).
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Information search and management skills.
Possess the capacity for decision-making.
Information literacy.
Develop critical reasoning.
Acquire commitment to ethics and social responsibility.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and permanent training.
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to work autonomously.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Know the different generations of computers from their beginnings to the present, as well as the most important figures in their evolution.

Theoretically understand the different numbering systems, the different parts of the computer, their functionality and interactivity, as well as the most basic concepts regarding programming, operating systems, and communications.
Enable the student to create documents with the word processor using advanced features needed to present assignments or reports in other subjects.
Understand the basic rudiments of using a spreadsheet and be able to create a simple presentation in PowerPoint or Prezzi.
Understand flow control structures in programming.
Understand the concept of function and modular decomposition.
Understand the basic software development process: editing, compilation, and execution.
Solve simple problems applying the previous concepts using pseudocode and flowcharts/ordinograms.
Be able to write very simple programming codes in terms of algorithmic difficulty.
Understand the internal functioning of an operating system at a very basic level: memory, process, and file structure management.
Understand the OSI communication model, types of networks, as well as the general functioning of the Internet.
Identify the need for information, select the most appropriate resources for its resolution, and manage it effectively as a necessary aspect for acquiring the course competencies.

syllabus_topics: Process, Memory, User, and File Management
Presentation of an Academic Work and Bibliographic References

assessment_methods.method: Practical computer tests and other continuous assessment activities on Office Automation content
Practical computer tests and other continuous assessment activities on Programming content
Final theoretical evaluation (excluding content from partial theoretical test)

assessment_rules: The final grade will be obtained by the weighted arithmetic mean of the procedures. To pass the course, a global score equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 is required. A minimum of 40% in the partial theoretical test, in each continuous assessment procedure for Office Automation, in each continuous assessment procedure for Programming, and in the final theoretical evaluation is required to pass the course. All failed tests in the 1st call can be recovered in the 2nd call, except for those that are impossible to repeat (which must be explicitly stated and justified). For students who fail in the 1st call, the procedures for the 2nd call will be the same, and they will not have to retake tests already passed in the 1st call.
